messages:
incident-bot: [PAGER] p99 streaming tail spike detected for service 'streaming-gen' in us-west-2. P95 120ms -> 600ms, P99 2.3s. Error rate low. Affected models: gptx-8q, gptx-4q. Triggering page to on-call.

sarah_ops: I'm on it. Looking at router metrics, there's a cluster of nodes in pool-gpu-15 with rising GPU temp and ECC correctables.

mike_oncall: Paging in. @sarah_ops please share node list and any active drains. I'll mute non-critical alerts once we confirm customer impact.

sarah_ops: Nodes: gpu-node-15a, gpu-node-15b, gpu-node-15c. gpu-node-15b showing repeated ECC_correctable spikes and thermal trip events. 15b reported throttle and driver reset 2x in last 3m.

anna_sre: Observing streaming stalls (clients stuck waiting for token frames). KV cache miss rates are normal. This looks like hardware-level stalls causing stalls in the runtime event loop. Rolling requests off 15b should help p99.

james_support: We've got live customer reports: support ticket INC-4432, user sees 'stream timing out' in prod app for about ~10% of requests. Not all customers, but major SaaS customer A affected.

elena_infra: Initiating coordinated drain of gpu-node-15b. Starting cordon + migrate active sessions with graceful fallback policy. Will move inflight sessions to 15a/15c then to CPU fallback if needed.

sarah_ops: Command to drain:
```
kubectl cordon gpu-node-15b
kubectl drain gpu-node-15b --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60
```
I'll monitor streaming backend logs for 'stall resume' markers.

deploy-bot: Deploy pipeline: scale up cpu-fallback-pool to +3 replicas (to accept spill) — action started.

mike_oncall: Can we temporarily route new sessions away from pool-gpu-15 entirely (soft-failover) while we warn customers and mitigate?

elena_infra: Yes, updating routing policy to avoid pool-gpu-15 for new traffic. Applying route: prefer pool-gpu-16, fallthrough to cpu-fallback.

anna_sre: After cordon+drain, p95 down to 140ms, p99 down to 650ms. Streaming stall count dropped by ~85% in the last 2 minutes. CPU fallback handling ~good, some increased cost but acceptable for mitigation window.

sarah_ops: Node 15b still shows intermittent ECC correctable bursts; recommend marking it for hardware inspection and permanent replace if further flake. Opening hardware ticket HD-782.

james_support: Notifying affected customer A with status update: partial degradation mitigated, engineers draining a degraded GPU node, ETA for full recovery unknown. Will offer temporary SKU credit.

mike_oncall: Thanks team. I'm going to update the incident channel and create an incident timeline. We'll hold until node is out of rotation and replacement scheduled.

incident-bot: Incident severity set to sev2. Escalation: oncall pager acknowledged by mike_oncall at 2139876550.

elena_infra: Post-mortem notes to collect: node telemetry (temps, ECC rates), driver/kernel logs, runtime stall traces, routing decision logs, and support ticket timeline.

sarah_ops: Adding follow-up tasks: (1) hardware RMA if flake persists, (2) add early-warning metric for ECC_correctable bursts tied to routing shift, (3) test drain playbook to ensure lower p99 impact.

mike_oncall: Closing handoff — I'll coordinate oncall follow-up. last check shows p99 stable at ~600ms and errors normalizing. Will re-open if regressions.

oncall-bot: Thread archived. If new alerts occur, create new page with context tag #gpu-degrade-2139876543.
